lesson.title: Loading the Right Cargo: Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetases
lesson.summary: Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases are enzymes that attach each amino acid to its correctly matching tRNA, the step where the accuracy of the entire genetic code is actually enforced.
lesson.body:
A tRNA arrives with an empty acceptor stem; something has to load the correct amino acid onto it before it is any use to a ribosome. That job belongs to a family of enzymes called aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, with roughly one dedicated synthetase for each of the twenty standard amino acids, though the exact count varies somewhat between organisms. Like any enzyme, each one catalyzes a specific reaction with a high degree of selectivity for its substrates; here, the substrates are one particular amino acid and the tRNA or small family of tRNAs whose anticodon corresponds to that amino acid.

The reaction itself uses energy from ATP. The synthetase binds its amino acid together with ATP, activates the amino acid, and then transfers it onto the 3' CCA end of the matching tRNA, forming a covalent bond and releasing AMP and pyrophosphate in the process. The product is called an aminoacyl-tRNA, or a charged tRNA, and it is this charged form, amino acid and tRNA joined together, that eventually gets delivered into the ribosome.

This is a more important checkpoint than it might first appear. Once a tRNA has been charged, the ribosome has no independent way to verify that the amino acid attached to it is actually correct; the ribosome simply reads the anticodon and trusts that whatever amino acid is riding along with it belongs there. That means the accuracy of the entire genetic code, the reliable link between a given codon and a given amino acid, depends almost entirely on the synthetase getting the pairing right in the first place. Correspondingly, these enzymes have proofreading mechanisms that check both the identity of the amino acid and the identity of the tRNA, using features like the anticodon itself along with parts of the acceptor stem, before committing to the attachment. A charged tRNA that passes this check is what shows up next at the ribosome's A site during elongation, ready to pair its anticodon against the next codon in line.
